patterns.reducedMotion: Disable timed cycling, keep the selected card static, and let users switch cards manually.
avoid: text over busy imagery without a scrim
copying travel footage or proprietary imagery

patterns.name: Responsive Hover Sidebar
patterns.useWhen: A project needs a dark collapsible sidebar where labels reveal on hover, focus, or explicit toggle, and active items are clear.
patterns.source: User-provided WhatsApp screenshot of a responsive sidebar clip with partial visible CSS.
implementationNotes: Labels must be available on hover, focus, and mobile, not hover-only.
Every nav target must be keyboard operable and have a visible active state.
On small screens, prefer the expanded readable state over icon-only navigation.
Use real route links or buttons wired to application state in production.
Keep source-video social UI and code frames out of previews.
patterns.reducedMotion: Remove width animation timing and reveal labels instantly while preserving focus order.

patterns.name: Glass Theme Pill Nav
patterns.useWhen: A project needs a warm glass pill navigation bar where an active capsule slides between items and a theme button changes the page mood.
patterns.source: User-provided WhatsApp screenshot of a glass pill nav and theme toggle clip with partial visible JavaScript.
implementationNotes: The active pill should move only after user selection, not autoplay.
Theme toggles must update CSS variables and then recalculate pill geometry.
Use enough contrast inside translucent glass surfaces.
Keep all targets large enough for touch and keyboard focus.
Do not use it as the only primary nav on dense enterprise screens without adaptation.
patterns.reducedMotion: Move the active pill instantly and keep the light/dark theme swap readable.
avoid: theme buttons with no real state change

patterns.name: Animated Delete Button
patterns.useWhen: A project needs a compact destructive-action button where the trash icon animates on click and resolves into a clear completed state.
patterns.source: User-provided WhatsApp screenshot of an animated delete button clip with partial visible HTML/SVG structure.
implementationNotes: Use only after confirmation when the action is truly destructive or irreversible.
Animate on click, not on page load.
Disable duplicate clicks while the action is pending.
Use server-confirmed success before showing permanent deleted state in production.
Keep animation short and provide reduced-motion behavior.
patterns.reducedMotion: Skip the trash/paper animation and update the label/state immediately after the action resolves.
avoid: triggering destructive work without confirmation when needed

patterns.name: SVG Path Particle Reveal
patterns.useWhen: A project needs an SVG silhouette, line-art path, moon, constellation, route, icon, or logo mark to scatter from depth and assemble into a premium particle shape.
patterns.source: User-provided JavaScript snippet that samples an SVG path with getTotalLength/getPointAtLength, creates THREE.Vector3 vertices, jitters them in x/y/z, and animates them from a centered origin with a GSAP timeline.
implementationNotes: Use owned, generated, open-source-permitted, or user-provided SVG paths only.
Normalize the SVG viewBox before mapping vertices into the scene; the captured 600 by 552 origin only applies to matching artwork.
For production Three.js, render sampled points with BufferGeometry and THREE.Points rather than one mesh per point.
Tune point density by device class; the captured 0.1 path step is dense and may be too heavy for mobile.
Use as a cinematic hero, loader, ambient background, logo reveal, or transition, not as critical navigation.
Keep source-video headings and code frames out of the preview UI; code belongs in files and metadata.
patterns.reducedMotion: Render the final path or logo as a static particle/shape image, skip the scatter timeline, and do not delay access to page content.
avoid: blocking auth, checkout, or data-entry flows
text placed directly on dense bright particles
visible code panels inside the design preview
